CommBrick::grow_send (src/comm_brick.cpp:1425-1438) allocates 'maxsend+bufextra' in all three flag branches, and src/comm.cpp:266-273 Comm::init_exchange sets 'maxexchange = maxexchange_atom + maxexchange_fix; bufextra = maxexchange + BUFEXTRA;' (BUFEXTRA = 1024, src/comm.h:34). The headroom is needed because CommBrick::exchange() tests 'if (nsend > maxsend) grow_send(nsend,1);' BEFORE packing one atom of up to maxexchange doubles at buf_send[nsend]. The legacy path does reach the KOKKOS allocator: src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.h:98 declares 'void grow_send(int, int) override;' and comm_kokkos.cpp:1846-1849 is 'void CommKokkos::grow_send(int n, int flag) { grow_send_kokkos(n,flag,Host); }', and CommKokkos::exchange() (1032-1043) falls through to CommBrick::exchange() whenever exchange_comm_legacy is set. What makes it latent: maxexchange_atom is 0 for every atom style except body (grep over src/*/atom_vec*.cpp shows only atom_vec_body.cpp:135 and the hybrid sum), because AtomVec only sets it when the size exceeds BUFEXTRA, and maxexchange_fix is 0 unless a fix sets it (fix neigh/history, fix store/atom, fix store/state, fix qtb/qbmsst, GRANSURF). So bufextra == BUFEXTRA in the common case and the two agree; the overflow needs maxexchange to exceed ~1024 minus the truncation remainder. The KOKKOS device exchange path is not affected because pack_exchange_kokkos re-grows k_buf_send itself (see the comment at comm_kokkos.cpp:1299).
fix: In src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1870 use the member instead of the constant and round up: 'int maxsend_border = (maxsend + bufextra + atomKK->avecKK->size_border - 1)/atomKK->avecKK->size_border;'. Comm::bufextra is a protected member kept current by Comm::init_exchange(), so it is directly accessible here. Apply the same rounding to grow_recv_kokkos line 1906 for consistency (that one needs no bufextra: CommBrick::grow_recv allocates only maxrecv).

reasoning: The defect and its location are real, but the failure mode is wrong: on a GPU build the sequence does not silently zero the coefficients, it makes Kokkos abort. Verified the code: allocate_kokkos() (dihedral_spherical_kokkos.cpp:457-501) takes the 'else' branch once allocated_kokkos is set and calls k_Ccoeff.resize(n+1,nterms_max) etc.; coeff() (516-551) refills only rows ilo..ihi of the host mirrors and then calls k_*.modify_host(); compute() (95-105) does k_*.sync<DeviceType>() on all of them. Traced the bundled DualView: impl_resize (lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:936-1032) picks 'if (modified_flags(1) >= modified_flags(0)) resize_on_device(arg_prop); else resize_on_host(arg_prop);' (1026-1031); resize_on_device (962-974) does Kokkos::resize on d_view (which preserves the old device data), then resync_host (1040-1049) 'h_view = create_mirror_view(typename t_host::memory_space(), d_view);' -- a fresh zero-initialized host allocation with NO copy back -- and then '++modified_flags(1)'. sync_impl (507-545) resets both flags to 0 after a successful copy, so after any 'run' the flags are 0/0 and the next resize does take the device branch. So far the finding is exactly right. Where it goes wrong is the next step: modify_host() (780-800) computes 'modified_flags(0) = max(f1,f0)+1' = 2 and then hits 'if (modified_flags(0) && modified_flags(1)) { ... Kokkos::abort("Kokkos::DualView::modify_host ERROR: Concurrent modification of host and device views ...") }'. With f1 == 1 from the resize, that condition is true, so the run dies loudly on the very first k_Ccoeff.modify_host() rather than continuing with zeroed coefficients. On a CPU-only build the whole thing is a no-op because impl_dualview_is_single_device is true (host and device memory spaces coincide): modify_host returns immediately, the flag increments are skipped and create_mirror_view returns d_view itself. Trigger is exactly as described: 'dihedral_coeff 1 ...; run N; dihedral_coeff 2 <more terms>' so that nterms_max grows and sizeMismatch is true. Same pattern, same bug, in src/KOKKOS/dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.cpp:349, src/KOKKOS/dihedral_fourier_kokkos.cpp:357-360 and src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:74-76.
fix: In allocate_kokkos()'s growth branch, stop using DualView::resize on views whose host mirror is not the authority. Either (a) re-create the DualViews exactly as the !allocated_kokkos branch does and then have coeff() refill every type 1..atom->ndihedraltypes from the base-class Ccoeff/phi_*/theta*_* arrays (what read_restart already does) rather than only rows ilo..ihi, or (b) call k_*.modify_host() on each view immediately before the resize so impl_resize takes the host-preserving resize_on_host branch, and still refill all types. Option (a) is the safer one and should be applied identically to dihedral_nharmonic_kokkos.cpp, dihedral_fourier_kokkos.cpp and angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp.

fix: Override write_restart()/restart() in FixTempCSLDKokkos to serialise the Kokkos pool: simplest correct approach is to keep a per-rank counter of how many states have been drawn (or store a derived re-seed) and re-seed rand_pool from it on restart, mirroring what the base does for RanMars. If that is not wanted, at minimum add a note to doc/src/fix_temp_csld.rst that the /kk variant does not restore its random-number state across a restart, and do the same for fix gjf/kk.

reasoning: Read both sides in full. src/CORESHELL/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs.cpp:107-108 first does 'rsq += EPSILON; r2inv = 1.0/rsq;', but inside the 'factor_coul < 1.0' analytic branch it REASSIGNS it at line 126 -- 'r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);' with the comment 'Additionally r2inv needs to be accordingly modified since the later scaling of the overall force shall be consistent' -- and that rescaled value is then what lines 152-157 use for the LJ term ('r6inv = r2inv*r2inv*r2inv; forcelj = r6inv*(lj1*r6inv - lj2); ... fpair = (forcecoul + factor_lj*forcelj) * r2inv;') and for evdwl further down. The KOKKOS port splits the two terms into independent helpers and only the Coulomb one learned about EPS_EWALD_SQR: compute_fpair (lines 194-211) and compute_evdwl (291-307) unconditionally do 'const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPSILON); const KK_FLOAT r2inv = 1.0/rsq;' with EPSILON = 1.0e-20 (line 54), and they receive neither factor_coul nor any flag, so they cannot branch; meanwhile compute_fcoul does get it right, returning 'forcecoul / (rsq_cs + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPS_EWALD_SQR))' at line 264. EPS_EWALD_SQR = 1.0e-12 (line 56), so for a special-bonded pair inside the coulomb cutoff the LJ r6inv differs from the CPU by (1e-12/1e-20)^3 = 1e24, exactly the 24 orders the finding claims. Practical impact is genuinely small: the divergence only appears for rsq comparable to or below 1e-12 (r < 1e-6), and typical core/shell inputs use special_bonds lj/coul 0 0 0 so factor_lj multiplies the LJ term to zero -- but that is also where the risk lies, because under a KK_FLOAT = float build r6inv = 1e60 overflows to inf and inf*0 is NaN, whereas the CPU's 1e36 stays finite in double.
fix: Give the LJ helpers the same information the Coulomb one has. Add the factor_coul (and cut_coulsq) arguments to PairLJCutCoulLongCSKokkos::compute_fpair and ::compute_evdwl and compute the denominator as 'const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + EPSILON + ((factor_coul < 1.0 && rsq_in + EPSILON < cut_coulsq) ? EPS_EWALD_SQR : 0.0);' before r2inv, matching src/CORESHELL/pair_lj_cut_coul_long_cs.cpp:126. If threading the extra arguments through pair_kokkos.h is undesirable, at least clamp r2inv to 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR) unconditionally, which reproduces the CPU value wherever it matters and removes the float overflow.
